headline: THE RUNWAY CATCHES PLANES
lede: The painted strip on Gullwing Isle was built for landings — until today only the glider could make one. Now the school plane answers it too: scrub speed, flare soft, and the deck catches you, scores you, and lets you go again.

notes.text: Plane touchdown is a real arrival: on-strip, sink under 2.2 m/s, below 34.5 m/s — and the zone table scores it SHORT 150 to FULL STRIP 700, same language as the glider. Hot (at cruise speed) still crashes: scrubbing with the stick is the skill the strip teaches.

After touchdown the hull rolls out; stick back at 16 m/s is a touch-and-go that climbs clear, and coasting to a stop hands her to the ground crew without a crash. Best landing banks to the ✈ WHEELS badge — the licence stays core-three, Pilotwings' landing-test card in all but name.
Proof: skywardcheck 118/118 (+14 pins) with all 36 mutants dead; skywardplay drives a live mid-strip catch (RUNWAY MIDDLE +300 banner) and a touch-and-go at :5178; contractcheck 857/857. Ship: #3327.

The old crash law splatted its own go-around — a climbing hull inside the deck window needed a 1.5 s departure grace, and live teleports must wait out the apron hand-off's respawn window before descending (lesson filed in STATE).
